findings.evidence: 20 queries, 10 should-trigger and 10 should-not-trigger, but no train/validation split and several positives name the skill's own objects (review-spec, --check-only, opencode) rather than a buried user intent.
findings.fix: Keep the 10/10 mix and near-misses, add a fixed ~60/40 train/validation split, and add should-trigger prompts that describe the outcome (pick review and coding models, order fallbacks) without naming config.toml, review-spec or --check-only.

findings.evidence: trust-local --show writes no trust record. It prints one line per project entry that runs as a subprocess.
findings.fix: State that --show records no trust but still runs cfg_migrate_project first, so a pending review-spec.toml is migrated before any JSON line, and point the agent at SKILL.md Step 4's pending-roster gate.

findings.evidence: detect-tools prints {"rg": bool, "sd": bool, "bat": bool, "eza": bool, "fd": bool, "codebase-memory-mcp": bool} — informational only, this step does not add new wizard questions.
findings.fix: Drop the detect-tools call and the instruction to mention those binaries later, or gate it on a step that actually consumes the result; record the removal.

findings.evidence: rejections is not currently consumed anywhere in this wizard flow — it's diagnostic output from fetch-model-catalog only; there is no step today that reads or acts on it.
findings.fix: Tell the agent to show each rejection reason beside its candidate and continue, or name the one condition that makes a rejection stop the proposal.

findings.evidence: Use when the user requests cross-AI review or execute setup, or when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers it because no lanes exist.
findings.fix: Cross-AI lane setup: detect installed CLIs and models, propose separate review and execute sets from the model catalog, ask each role's order, effort and opt-in flags, and write the [lanes] table of ai-kit's config.toml. Use when the user wants to choose, check or refresh review or coding lanes, order fallbacks, or replace an old review-spec.toml, even if they never say lanes or config.toml, and when ai-kit-spec-review or ai-kit-spec-execute-superpowers offers setup because no lanes exist. Writes ./.aikit/config.toml by default, asks before replacing an existing roster, and supports --check-only, --local and --global. Not for running a review or executing a plan with lanes that already exist, editing [runner] or other tables, or writing secrets.env.
Change the NEVER example to the literal purpose values the writer accepts, review, execute and both, and say translating them to REVIEW or EXECUTE writes the lane into the wrong role.

findings.evidence: Set up (or refresh) ai-kit-spec-review's cross-AI reviewer configuration.
findings.fix: Replace that sentence with the task the body actually performs: write both the review and execute lane sets; move it only if a later edit depends on the old wording, and record the removal.
